A1.label: PlayArea.on_control_focus_entered — mouse hover grabs focus, so focus is the ONE hover signal for mouse, keyboard and pad

A3.label: PlayArea._show_focus_info — a 260 px panel pinned beside the card, re-pinned every frame

A4.label: PlayArea._on_gui_input — left click on the focused card

A5.label: PlayArea._info_mode true, so info_requested carries card_info instead of data_selected — the click performs NO game action

A8.label: InfoCard.show_entry — the ONE notecard, anchored to the bottom of the WINDOW

A9.label: Main._on_info_toggled — the camera animates to WallPicture.info_zoom_state

A10.label: Map._on_node_hovered — MapHoverPanel.get_info, published and nothing else

B1.label: NEW — a highlight arrives: mouse hover, or keyboard and pad selection. Same rule for both

B2.label: NEW — the container swaps its contents to the description, instantly, no animation — chart C

B3.label: NEW — an ARMED card alone does NOT open it. Arming is not highlighting, and it moves no focus — chart G

B4.label: NEW — pointer leaves everything with nothing locked: the description STAYS, showing the last entry, so it never blinks in and out

B5.label: NEW — a click on a card LOCKS the description to it, and the same click still performs its game action — chart E

B6.label: NEW — locked, and the pointer moves to another card

B7.label: NEW — the description follows the hover, and returns to the locked card once the pointer leaves everything

B8.label: NEW — locking a second card replaces the first. Only one lock exists

B10.label: NEW — dismissing REVERTS the container to the HUD. Nothing is hidden, because the container is always on screen

B11.label: NEW — the held card leaves the bounds of the cell it came from — but ONLY once it is FOLLOWING, so an untouched armed card never closes a description by accident, and NEVER for a card the player CLICKED to lock: that one click both locked and grabbed it, so its placement is what closes it — `GAP-008`=a

B12.label: NEW — the card is placed: the interaction is finished, so the description closes

B13.label: NEW — a board rebuild keeps the same CardData's description, whichever control now represents it

B14.label: NEW — the win or lose screen leaves the description open, so a card can still be read beside the result

B15.label: NEW — leaving the screen closes it, and each screen REMEMBERS its own last description

B16.label: NEW — coming back re-shows that description immediately, exactly as it was left

B17.label: NEW — Game.processing goes TRUE: the container reverts to the HUD whatever was showing, INCLUDING a locked description — chart C

B18.label: NEW — that lock is gone for good. It is not restored when processing ends

B19.label: NEW — hovers DURING processing are ignored entirely, so a resting pointer cannot swap the HUD straight back out

B20.label: NEW — processing ends, and the HUD STAYS until any focus event at all, including focus landing back on the card it was already on

C1.label: NEW — one real PanelContainer with a flat background and no border. Art later; the container is what makes art possible

C3.label: NEW — inside the HUD, top to bottom: the numbers first, then the piles as one ROW across the width, then the actions

C4.label: NEW — members: Deck, Discard, Rules, Goal, Total, Combo, Undo, End. %MultScore and %Preview are DELETED in the same pass — chart L

C5.label: NEW — a highlight arrives, so the contents swap to the description, its preview drawn at the size the highlighted object is itself drawn at: the board's card size from the board, each viewer's own from that viewer (GAP-004=b) — chart B

C6.label: NEW — while the description shows, the HUD's controls are off screen. Accepted

C7.label: NEW — a LOCKED description is forced back to the HUD by cancel

C8.label: NEW — Game.processing forces it back too, lock and all, and the HUD is then what the player watches the cascade in: the score, the goal and the combo are what the cascade animates

C9.label: NEW — the HUD holds until ANY focus event once processing ends

C10.label: NEW — the processing rule is the GAME screen only. The map has no cascade worth watching — chart K

C11.label: NEW — the panel eats clicks in its whole rect, which today's scattered controls do not

C12.label: NEW — no hud_scale. The container lays out to its own rect, so the scale mechanism and both authored-offset caches go — chart L

C13.label: NEW — the MAP gets the same container, holding Fame, Lap, Luck and its Deck button, and both screens convert its window px through their own picture, which is what makes the geometry identical (GAP-003=a)

C14.label: The debug bar and the prop-step controls stay OUTSIDE it, top-right, unchanged

C15.label: GameView win or lose overlay still covers ONLY the play area, so the container stays live

C16.label: NEW — the exit X in the container's top-right means GO BACK TO THE HUD, sized by the same touch-target rule as every other overlay control — chart M

D1.label: NEW — ONE knob: the container's width as a fraction of the WINDOW. hud_width_fraction is retired

D2.label: NEW — would the play area LEFT OVER be taller than it is wide

D3.label: NEW — the container is on the LEFT, full window height

D4.label: NEW — the container moves to the TOP, where the HUD also is, so the main playing window stays as square as possible

D5.label: NEW — at the top the same fraction is read as a HEIGHT

D6.label: NEW — is the window more extreme in SHAPE than the project's reference window, which is what makes the maximum apply at all (GAP-001=b), and does the fraction exceed it

D7.label: NEW — clamped, and the clamp is measured INWARD: the container sits flush against the inner edge of its band, so it stays near the middle and the empty space is on its far side

D8.label: NEW — PlayArea.board_inset_left becomes the container's width, converted from window pixels to picture pixels through the focused picture's live scale, plus the crop that covering scale puts off-window on that axis (GAP-002=a)

D9.label: NEW — a matching TOP inset exists for the case where the container moved up, and matching RIGHT and BOTTOM edges for the crop, so the board's region is the VISIBLE picture

D10.label: NEW — the board centres in what is left, never on the screen — and what is left is what the player can SEE beside the container

D11.label: The MAP converts exactly as the board does: window px through the map picture's live cover scale and through the map camera's own zoom (GAP-003=a)

D12.label: NEW — the overlay's Back, Forward and Wall buttons draw ON TOP of the container and stay pressable

D13.label: InfoCard._reposition_to_window — the same re-anchor on resize, keeping its content

D14.label: NEW — the container does NOT pan with the board. GameView._process's furniture slide and PlayArea.pan_window_left_x are both deleted — chart L

E1.label: NEW — what is under the press

E2.label: NEW — an ENTRANCE card: re-arms it AND locks its description, in one click

E3.label: NEW — a CELL, and is a card armed

E4.label: NEW — armed: the card is placed immediately, one click, no confirm — and on touch too, because it is undoable and hesitation is worse

E6.label: NEW — occupied: the card STACKS, and the highlight already showed whether it would — an occupied cell offers the card on TOP as the target, so it is marked only while a rule accepts that (GAP-005=a)

E7.label: NEW — nothing armed: the click opens that cell's description if it holds a card

E8.label: NEW — a BOARD card: a CLICK still needs the armed card cancelled first, or the click would try to place onto it instead

E9.label: NEW — if the board card is not stackable, picking it up is the only remaining action, so the grab is allowed straight away

E10.label: NEW — a DRAG from a board card cancels the arm implicitly, because a drag is unambiguous about which card is being moved

E11.label: NEW — while a board card is held, the Entrance DISARMS until it is put down

E12.label: NEW — the press was released — how far did it travel

E13.label: NEW — within the threshold: it was a CLICK. The card is grabbed and stays held — chart M for the threshold

E14.label: NEW — beyond it: the RELEASE places, on both mouse and touch. One gesture model for every device

E16.label: Game.place_card_in_grid — a LEGAL cell only, and the highlight is literally the drop map: it is swept through the same on_can_place_stack dispatch try_place uses (GAP-005=a)

E17.label: NEW — anywhere else, the container included and off-window included: the card goes back to its slot, still armed, still lifted, no longer following. A failed drag costs nothing. The return HOLDS: only a new press starts it following again, never a mouse motion (GAP-007=a)

E18.label: NEW — a drag-placed card is an ordinary undo step and commits the Entrance to its grid exactly as a clicked one does. Nothing downstream can tell which route was taken

E20.label: NEW — the HELD CARD is released first

E21.label: NEW — a second press then dismisses the description — chart B

E22.label: NEW — Escape does MORE than cancel: it cancels everything the second button would AND shows the menu or wall immediately

E23.label: NEW — on a touchscreen the FIRST tap behaves as a hover, so nothing commits on it

E24.label: NEW — and a touch TAP needs no threshold of its own: a release on the card's own slot is not a placeable spot, so it goes back to exactly where it already was

F1.label: Godot delivers an ORDINARY click first: Windows sends WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK in place of the second press, so by the time a tap is recognised the card is already grabbed

F2.label: NEW — the tap UNDOES that first click's grab

F3.label: NEW — a tap arriving after a PLACEMENT is refused outright. A placement can never be rewound by a double-click

F4.label: NEW — on touch the project detects the double-tap itself, from two screen presses within a time window and a distance window, because Godot never sets double_tap on a Windows touchscreen

F5.label: NEW — on keyboard and pad, BOTH: a double-press of the normal button, and a separate bindable action of its own

F6.label: NEW — a double-click on an ENTRANCE card taps it, and the arm still stands

F7.label: NEW — an empty cell's zone card taps too, because zone cards carry modifiers

F8.label: NEW — a tapped signal is emitted. Nothing in the game listens in v1 except one dummy effect built for testing

F9.label: NEW — the second mouse button is cancel-only. It no longer taps, which is what DESIGN_DOC section 12 originally planned — chart E

G1.label: NEW — the LEFTMOST card present in the Entrance arms automatically, matching the refill's own left-to-right order

G2.label: NEW — arming calls Game.try_grab and PlayArea.grab_cards, the SAME functions a player pickup calls, with no flag and no second path

G3.label: NEW — and it moves NO focus and NO selection highlight. Nothing to suppress on the description side, because no highlight moved — chart B

G4.label: NEW — the card LIFTS the moment it arms, to show it is selected and about to move. That lift is the first thing a fresh board shows

G5.label: NEW — but it does NOT follow the cursor yet

G7.label: NEW — any mouse motion at all, including the one Godot emulates from a touch. No threshold. A key or pad focus does NOT start it: the card stays lifted in its slot and the pad player places by accept on a cell (GAP-006=b)

G8.label: NEW — now it follows, at the same lift height, so the only visible change is that it starts moving. Following is a ONE-WAY latch until the card is placed or cancelled

G9.label: NEW — GLOW means selected. LIFT means currently picked up, warning that the next click on a highlighted space will put it down. The selection glow sits wherever the selector is

G10.label: NEW — focus RESTS on the armed card once, at the start of a show only. After that the two move independently

G11.label: NEW — a card the player CLICKS follows immediately: the mouse has just moved by definition. The delay only ever applies to a card nobody touched

G12.label: NEW — every legal cell's own zone card has its FACE brightened toward white by highlight_glow in player_settings.gd, the rank, suit, stamp and art excluded, re-swept when the hand or the board changes. Nothing is lit until the player lifts a card, so the map is on for as long as one is in hand. The FOCUS is a separate mark and never brightens: it draws the card's outer rim in the match ink (GAP-005=a, R6)

G13.label: Game.place_card_in_grid — the placement commits the Entrance to its grid. Arming commits nothing

G14.label: NEW — after a placement, and after a refill, the new leftmost present card arms — chart I

G15.label: NEW — cancel DISARMS, and clicks on cells then do nothing until something is armed again

G16.label: NEW — the arm is view-only. Undo restores the board and the arm is re-derived as leftmost present

G17.label: NEW — keyboard and pad: the arm replaces the old select-an-Entrance-card step, and the arrows go straight to aiming a cell cursor

G18.label: NEW — every slot's stock empty: nothing arms, and clicks on cells do nothing — chart H

H1.label: NEW — each Entrance slot owns its OWN ordered stock. The single draw deck is replaced by them

H2.label: Game.shuffle_deck — the one shuffle the game already does, unchanged

H3.label: NEW — the shuffled deck is DEALT round-robin, left to right, so earlier slots take the extras when the count does not divide

H4.label: NEW — this happens at show start, and again whenever the SET of slots changes

H5.label: NEW — no new RNG anywhere, so the resume-replay ruling holds exactly as it does today

H7.label: NEW — a slot was REMOVED: its cards go from ITS BOTTOM, round-robin, to the BOTTOMS of the remaining slots, left to right

H8.label: NEW — a slot was ADDED: the bottom card of each existing slot in turn, round-robin, until the new slot has its even share

H9.label: NEW — TOPS NEVER MOVE. What is about to be drawn is stable, so a peek effect stays honest

H10.label: NEW — the rebalance is silent. It is bookkeeping under face-down cards and nothing visible moves

H11.label: NEW — a slot whose stock exhausts stays empty. Exhaustion never triggers a rebalance

H12.label: NEW — no caller adds or removes a slot yet. This is machinery built for a future card effect, deliberately with no caller today

H13.label: NEW — stocks are part of the board: on_append and every board walk reach their cards exactly as they reach the draw deck today

H14.label: NEW — an in-flight save written before this change is DISCARDED, not migrated

H15.label: Game.return_to_map — the discard is still swept back only when the show ends

I1.label: Game.refill_entrance_if_due — the trigger is unchanged: the Entrance is empty, OR no held card has a legal placement

I2.label: TypeInput.on_refill — each header still fills its own slot if that slot is empty, left to right by dispatch order

I3.label: NEW — the card comes off the top of THAT SLOT'S OWN STOCK — chart H

I4.label: NEW — every slot holding a face-down card FLIPS IT UP IN PLACE, staggered left to right to match the draw order

I5.label: NEW — the stagger is a knob, as a fraction of get_delay per slot, never a wall-clock literal

I6.label: NEW — slots still holding a face-up card do NOTHING. Only empty slots flip

I7.label: NEW — there is no fly-in from the Deck control any more

I8.label: NEW — owner ruling at S21: a non-empty stock shows exactly ONE face-down card under the revealed card, drawn with frame 3 of the card sheet; no other stock card is an entity. At a refill it flips up to become the revealed card and a fresh face-down appears beneath while the stock has cards. No cap, no knob

I9.label: NEW — a slot with nothing left shows an empty slot frame, which is what the Entrance already shows

I10.label: NEW — hovering a face-down stock describes the SLOT, not a card: how many remain in this stock — chart B

I11.label: NEW — a bonus reveal simply DEEPENS that slot's face-up stack, since the Entrance already holds a stack per slot

I12.label: NEW — the Deck button shows the union of every stock as ONE list, sorted by suit and rank so no ordering leaks

J1.label: Game.place_card_in_grid — a placement resolves: every line scored, every prop tick finished

J2.label: GameData.has_met_goal — the check fires once the WHOLE placement has settled, never mid-cascade

J3.label: NEW — the Goal label changes state the moment the total passes it, so the ending is announced rather than sprung

J4.label: NEW — a short pause, so the final score lands visibly

J5.label: Game.end_show — the same flag, the same save, the same resolve the End button drives today

J6.label: NEW — there is no declining. Reaching the goal ends the show, full stop

J7.label: Game.exit_show — Continue still banks the fame, so the outcome stays undoable

J8.label: NEW — the End button SURVIVES, for a show that can no longer be won

J9.label: NEW — End is REVEALED when either the deck is empty, or no more action is possible on the board

J10.label: A full board still does NOT end a show: cards may remain in the Entrance and effects may free cells

J11.label: Game.undo — rewinds an automatic end exactly as it rewinds a manual one, back to the live board

J12.label: Resume lands on the outcome screen, because show_ended is saved before the resolve

J13.label: NEW — the outcome screen carries its own Undo beside Continue, in the same SubViewport, so a d-pad walks Continue ↔ Undo. Focus navigation never crosses a viewport and no undo action is bound, so the HUD's Undo is mouse-only from here; it stays where it is, and Undo shows twice while the outcome is up (GAP-009=b)

K2.label: NEW — a small popup appears with the node's NAME ONLY, directly above the node, centred, and it stays put

K3.label: OVERTURNED by the first playtest ruling — a hover NAMES only; a CLICK picks the node and fills the sidebar, so the description and the Travel button can never aim at different nodes — chart B

K4.label: OVERTURNED by the first playtest ruling — a click PICKS and travels nowhere; a Travel button beside the description is the one way there, so a node can be previewed before it is chosen

K5.label: OVERTURNED by the first playtest ruling — a tap picks, and no tap count travels: a finger uses the Travel button too

K6.label: NEW — after the pointer leaves, the sidebar keeps the last node's description, the same persistence the board has

K7.label: MapHoverPanel.get_info — the entry is now ALWAYS used, so the old build-and-throw-away waste is gone

K8.label: OVERTURNED by the first playtest ruling — the sidebar is too narrow to read a pack in: the first pick of a pack node lists its possible cards in a viewer instead, and a button beside the description asks for that list again

K9.label: RETIRED with K8 — there is no grid inside the sidebar to pick out of, so there is no way back either

K10.label: NEW — keyboard and pad: a node cursor, and whatever is selected is described. Same rule as the board

K11.label: NEW — no small popup on the board. It is a map affordance, for nodes that are just dots

K12.label: NEW — the sidebar is on the same side as the game's, always — chart D

L1.label: wall_info_mode, the wall_info InputMap action, and the overlay's magnifying-glass Info toggle

L2.label: WallPicture.info_zoom_state and WallTransition's info branch — the zoom-out goes with them

L5.label: Tools/wall_editor.tscn's Info panel becomes a SIDEBAR preview panel: width, side, opacity and the exit X, live against a real hosted screen

L6.label: Tests/Wall/test_wall_info and Tests/Visual/wall_info_snapshot are REPLACED by sidebar equivalents, so coverage does not drop

L8.label: GameView._process's furniture pan, its two authored-offset caches, hud_scale, and PlayArea.pan_window_left_x

L9.label: %MultScore with its Col, x and Row children, and %Preview

L10.label: hud_width_fraction, replaced by the container's own window fraction — chart D

L11.label: The deck, discard and rules viewers' own description panels, which publish to the sidebar instead

L12.label: GameData.draw_deck as the single deck, replaced by per-slot stocks — chart H

L13.label: UI/deck_builder.gd is REPAIRED, not deleted: new classes, dead code removed, the tool itself kept

L14.label: WallInput.mm_to_px, and every millimetre knob: grid_swipe_threshold_mm with its _min_mm and _max_mm, wall_touch_target_mm, and the wall_touch_target_min_px and _max_px bounds — chart M

L15.label: card_tap_slop_mm never ships at all: one basis covers every gesture this design introduces

M1.label: NEW — NO DPI READING SURVIVES ANYWHERE. Both consumers go, and the reason is measured: a DPI reading is unreliable on multi-monitor Windows, which reports the primary screen's for all of them, and on Android

M2.label: NEW — is this how far you must MOVE, or how big a thing must be to HIT

M3.label: NEW — MOVE: a fraction of the CARD's current on-screen size, so the gesture scales with the thing being dragged and is right at every board zoom

M4.label: NEW — a knob, defaulting to a quarter of the card's width

M5.label: NEW — a gesture with no card under it, such as a swipe on bare board, uses the default card size at the current zoom, so there is always a reference

M6.label: PlayArea._swipe_threshold_px — the board swipe moves onto this basis too, so the game has one answer rather than two

M7.label: NEW — HIT: a fraction of the WINDOW's smaller dimension, the one reference every screen has, because the overlay lives outside the board where no card exists

M8.label: NEW — a knob defaulting to 6 per cent, with NO clamp: the fraction IS the clamp, since it cannot run away the way a DPI reading could

M9.label: WallInput.touch_target_px — the NAME survives with a new body, so every caller keeps the seam it already uses

M10.label: WallOverlay._apply_touch_targets — still mandatory, and still on PICTURE_WALL.md's wiring contract. Only what it computes changes

M11.label: NEW — the sidebar's exit X follows the same rule as every other overlay control

M12.label: NEW — this formally reverses Q123 in picture-wall, which chose 9 mm physical derived from the reported DPI. That answer is shipped code, and it is the one superseded answer in this design that reaches another
